news.title: Frank Elderson: Ensuring resilience in the face of uncertainty
U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

news.title: Christine Lagarde: IMFC Statement
U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

news.title: Christine Lagarde: IMFC Statement
U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

news.title: Christine Lagarde: IMFC Statement
U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

news.title: Christine Lagarde: IMFC Statement
U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

news.summary: Headline inflation increased to 3.8% in September, mostly reflecting a surge in energy inflation, and, to a lesser extent, an increase in food and services inflation. The Governing Council decided to raise the key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points in September, following an increase of the same size in June. The September ECB staff projections foresee growth of 0.9% in 2026, 1.4% in 2027 and 1.5% in 2028. Looking ahead, higher energy prices are expected to keep headline inflation well above target into the first half of 2027 and to gradually feed through to core and food inflation.

news.title: Christine Lagarde: IMFC Statement
news.summary: Headline inflation increased to 3.8% in September, mostly reflecting a surge in energy inflation, and, to a lesser extent, an increase in food and services inflation. The Governing Council decided to raise the key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points in September, following an increase of the same size in June. The September ECB staff projections foresee growth of 0.9% in 2026, 1.4% in 2027 and 1.5% in 2028. Looking ahead, higher energy prices are expected to keep headline inflation well above target into the first half of 2027 and to gradually feed through to core and food inflation.

news.title: U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

news.title: Software’s new consolidator gets big vote of confidence from Berkshire
news.summary: In its first earnings report as a public company in August, Bending Spoons said revenue more than doubled from a year earlier to over $700 million, with growth almost entirely driven by acquisitions, while net income climbed 171% to $177 million. In August, Bending Spoons announced it was buying workflow software provider Airtable for about $1.3 billion, or almost 90% below the company's peak valuation from late 2021. Berkshire, which Bending Spoons describes as a "longstanding inspiration" for its strategy, has now invested over $900 million in the company, including a $330 million stake disclosed on Wednesday. Wall Street loved the deal, sending Bending Spoons' stock up 41%, though some of those gains were lost later in the week, leaving the company with a market cap of about $30 billion.

news.title: Christine Lagarde: IMFC Statement
news.summary: Headline inflation increased to 3.8% in September, mostly reflecting a surge in energy inflation, and, to a lesser extent, an increase in food and services inflation. The Governing Council decided to raise the key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points in September, following an increase of the same size in June. The September ECB staff projections foresee growth of 0.9% in 2026, 1.4% in 2027 and 1.5% in 2028. Looking ahead, higher energy prices are expected to keep headline inflation well above target into the first half of 2027 and to gradually feed through to core and food inflation.

news.title: U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

news.title: Category 2 Hurricane Isaias nears landfall, leading to production shut-ins
news.summary: As of 4:00 a.m. central time on October 9, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration expects Hurricane Isaias to make landfall on the Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, creating the potential for significant disruptions to energy infrastructure. Hurricane Isaias is the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season and will be the largest storm system to make landfall in the region since Hurricane Helene in September 2024.

news.title: Why hedge funds could be making a bond market shock more likely
news.summary: Hedge funds held a record 7% of the $30 trillion Treasury market at the end of 2025, according to U.S. Earlier this month, 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields hit their highest levels since 2002. Breeden — the central bank's deputy governor for financial stability, and a member of its rates-setting Monetary Policy Committee — said the changing mix of bond market investors, and their increased use of leverage, raises the risk of localized market turbulence turning into broader financial stress. Across the Atlantic, yields on 10-year U.K. government bonds , known as gilts, also touched multi-decade highs.

Revealed: VW, Ford and Tesla batteries linked to destructive deforestation of indigenous lands
news.summary: Mines in supply chains of western carmakers linked to widespread deforestation of primary rainforest in nickel-rich lands inhabited by Tolaki people in Indonesia Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla are among the electric carmakers whose batteries may contain nickel mined in indigenous woodlands plagued by deforestation, an analysis has found, highlighting the struggle to make vehicles that are free from environmental destruction. Corporate disclosures and trade flows from the last two years show mines in the battery supply chains of automotive giants are linked to the loss of trees in Sulawesi, a wildlife hotspot in Indonesia that houses the world’s largest nickel deposits. The metal is widely used in cathodes in car batteries because it boosts energy density and increases range.

news.title: Christine Lagarde: IMFC Statement
news.summary: Headline inflation increased to 3.8% in September, mostly reflecting a surge in energy inflation, and, to a lesser extent, an increase in food and services inflation. The Governing Council decided to raise the key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points in September, following an increase of the same size in June. The September ECB staff projections foresee growth of 0.9% in 2026, 1.4% in 2027 and 1.5% in 2028. Looking ahead, higher energy prices are expected to keep headline inflation well above target into the first half of 2027 and to gradually feed through to core and food inflation.

news.title: U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

news.title: Revealed: VW, Ford and Tesla batteries linked to destructive deforestation of indigenous lands
news.summary: Mines in supply chains of western carmakers linked to widespread deforestation of primary rainforest in nickel-rich lands inhabited by Tolaki people in Indonesia Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla are among the electric carmakers whose batteries may contain nickel mined in indigenous woodlands plagued by deforestation, an analysis has found, highlighting the struggle to make vehicles that are free from environmental destruction. Corporate disclosures and trade flows from the last two years show mines in the battery supply chains of automotive giants are linked to the loss of trees in Sulawesi, a wildlife hotspot in Indonesia that houses the world’s largest nickel deposits. The metal is widely used in cathodes in car batteries because it boosts energy density and increases range.

news.title: Christine Lagarde: IMFC Statement
news.summary: Headline inflation increased to 3.8% in September, mostly reflecting a surge in energy inflation, and, to a lesser extent, an increase in food and services inflation. The Governing Council decided to raise the key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points in September, following an increase of the same size in June. The September ECB staff projections foresee growth of 0.9% in 2026, 1.4% in 2027 and 1.5% in 2028. Looking ahead, higher energy prices are expected to keep headline inflation well above target into the first half of 2027 and to gradually feed through to core and food inflation.

news.title: U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. Even though it is in a region with lower solar resources, New York ranks as the fifth-largest rooftop solar generation producer as a result of capacity growth supported by technology improvements and state incentives.

news.title: Revealed: VW, Ford and Tesla batteries linked to destructive deforestation of indigenous lands
news.summary: Mines in supply chains of western carmakers linked to widespread deforestation of primary rainforest in nickel-rich lands inhabited by Tolaki people in Indonesia Volkswagen, Ford and Tesla are among the electric carmakers whose batteries may contain nickel mined in indigenous woodlands plagued by deforestation, an analysis has found, highlighting the struggle to make vehicles that are free from environmental destruction. Corporate disclosures and trade flows from the last two years show mines in the battery supply chains of automotive giants are linked to the loss of trees in Sulawesi, a wildlife hotspot in Indonesia that houses the world’s largest nickel deposits. The metal is widely used in cathodes in car batteries because it boosts energy density and increases range.

news.summary: Headline inflation increased to 3.8% in September, mostly reflecting a surge in energy inflation, and, to a lesser extent, an increase in food and services inflation. The Governing Council decided to raise the key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points in September, following an increase of the same size in June. news.title: U.S. small-scale solar generation has quadrupled in the last decade
news.summary: We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade. The four states with the highest generation of small-scale solar in the country-California, Arizona, Texas, and Florida-are in regions with more abundant solar resources. news.summary: Climate shocks can also affect food prices: ECB research estimates that the extreme summer heat in 2022 increased food prices in Europe by around 0.7 percentage points over the following months. It was the warmest summer ever recorded in Western Europe, marked by severe droughts, devastating wildfires, water scarcity and mounting pressure on ecosystems across the continent. [ 1 ] Water levels in major European rivers fell to exceptionally low levels, affecting transport, industry and energy production. news.title: King acknowledges 'suffering of the past' as Caribbean tour begins
news.summary: Prior to the trip, Buckingham Palace said the King would not shy away from "colonial legacy" and the impact of the slave trade during his visit but, in line with the UK government position, he will not apologise for Britain's role in the slave trade or offer reparations. news.title: Frank Elderson: Taking action for nature – investing in economic resilience and prosperity
news.summary: The European Commission estimates that, if current levels of PFAS pollution in Europe continue until 2050, the cost to society could reach €440 billion over that period. Treating polluted water alone could cost more than €1 trillion. [ 7 ] And the effects differ across regions and sectors: agriculture here, manufacturing there and energy production somewhere else. A landmark report by the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform , published this year and approved by more than 150 member governments, warns that biodiversity loss is among the most serious threats to businesses. UNEP's State of Finance for Nature 2026 estimates that annual investment in nature-based solutions needs to reach $571 billion by 2030, compared with approximately $220 billion in 2023.

news.title: October 2026 euro area bank lending survey
news.summary: According to the October 2026 bank lending survey (BLS), euro area banks reported a further net tightening of credit standards – banks’ internal guidelines or loan approval criteria – for loans or credit lines to enterprises in the third quarter of 2026 (net percentage of 9% of banks; Chart 1). In the third quarter of 2026, euro area banks reported a net decrease in demand for loans or credit lines to firms (net percentage of -6%; Chart 2).

news.summary: Core inflation indicators -- obtained by removing transitory disturbances and institutional factors from the actual movements observed in the consumer prices -- are frequently used for inflation analysis. news.title: Four takeaways from Anthropic’s potentially record-breaking stock market filing
news.summary: The AI company’s first public financial disclosures reveal explosive growth, huge costs and risks ranging from cyber-attacks to the limits of safeguards Anthropic has filed to go public on the US stock market, revealing for the first time the AI research lab’s financials and all the risks – more than 90 pages of them – that might negatively affect its business. The filing to US financial regulators, known as an S-1, provides the public’s first look at an audited version of Anthropic’s finances. The company’s investor prospectus, released on Monday, veers from hyperbolic predictions about AI’s “incredible potential” to existential risks of the technology to the reality of its current business: explosive but incredibly expensive growth.

news.summary: According to the October 2026 bank lending survey (BLS), euro area banks reported a further net tightening of credit standards – banks’ internal guidelines or loan approval criteria – for loans or credit lines to enterprises in the third quarter of 2026 (net percentage of 9% of banks; Chart 1). Banks reported unchanged credit standards for loans to households for house purchase (net percentage of 0%) and a further net tightening for consumer credit and other lending to households (net percentage of 14%). For firms, the net tightening surpassed the expectations reported by banks in the previous survey round (5%). In the third quarter of 2026, euro area banks reported a net decrease in demand for loans or credit lines to firms (net percentage of -6%; Chart 2).

news.title: Fed holds interest rates steady in last decision before midterms
news.summary: US central bank last month raised rates for first time since 2023, in move that infuriated Donald Trump The US Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged on Wednesday during its last board meeting before the midterm elections, keeping rates at one of the highest pre-election levels seen in over 20 years. Last month, Fed officials raised rates for the first time since 2023, citing rising inflation, bringing rates to a range of 3.75% to 4. Inflation has hovered for years above the Fed’s target rate of 2%, and for most of this year, the annualized inflation rate has remained above 3%. Two board members voted against the pause, preferring to raise rates by a quarter point this meeting, the Fed said in a statement.

news.title: Why China is desperate to ship cars outside of the country
news.summary: For the full year 2026, China's domestic passenger car retail sales are set to drop 22% to 18.5 million vehicles, the association said — under the level recorded in the first year of the pandemic. Passenger car retail sales for 2026 in China totaled 13.33 million units through September, falling 21.7% from a year ago, according to the China Passenger Car Association. Gasoline car sales have been declining in China because of the country's transition to electric vehicles, but sales in China of new-energy vehicles — which includes EVs — dropped by 12.8% from January through September, according to the association. Industrial profits for the first nine months of the year were up 15.5% from the same period in 2025, but September showed signs of weakness relative to the prior eight months, according to China's National Bureau of Statistics .

news.title: Survey on the Access to Finance of Enterprises: lending conditions tightened
news.summary: Similarly, firms’ median inflation expectations remained broadly unchanged among firms that took part in both the current and previous survey rounds, whereas they rose significantly in the full sample (Chart 4). In the most recent round of the Survey on the Access to Finance of Enterprises (SAFE) in the euro area, covering the third quarter of 2026, euro area firms widely reported a further net increase in interest rates on bank loans (net 46%, compared with 42% in the previous quarter). Large firms reported increases more often (net 55%, up from 41%) than small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) (net 38%, down from 43%). At the same time, a net 27% of firms (down from 31% in the previous quarter) reported increases in other financing costs (i.e. charges, fees and commissions) and in collateral requirements (net 14%, up from 10%) (Chart 1).

news.title: Bessent says 'not necessarily' a mistake if the Fed hikes again
news.summary: Bessent said he would like to see the Fed have an "open mind" about the supply shock from energy prices having a "transitory nature." The U.S. war with Iran has led to a sharp drop in global crude production volumes, in turn leading annual inflation readings to move further from the Fed's target of 2%. Bessent also said the U.S. efforts to isolate the Iran economy, dubbed Operation Economic Outcast , have been "very successful." He said internal estimates show that Iran's economy could contract by as much as 25% in the span of a year. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday that further Federal Reserve rate hikes wouldn't necessarily be a mistake. After CNBC's Brian Sullivan asked if rate increases in the future would constitute a monetary policy error, Bessent responded: "That's not necessarily so." Bessent's comments came hours after the Fed announced it would keep interest rates unchanged at its October gathering, as the market widely expected.

news.title: Why China is desperate to ship cars outside of the country
news.summary: For the full year 2026, China's domestic passenger car retail sales are set to drop 22% to 18.5 million vehicles, the association said — under the level recorded in the first year of the pandemic. Passenger car retail sales for 2026 in China totaled 13.33 million units through September, falling 21.7% from a year ago, according to the China Passenger Car Association. Gasoline car sales have been declining in China because of the country's transition to electric vehicles, but sales in China of new-energy vehicles — which includes EVs — dropped by 12.8% from January through September, according to the association. Industrial profits for the first nine months of the year were up 15.5% from the same period in 2025, but September showed signs of weakness relative to the prior eight months, according to China's National Bureau of Statistics .

news.title: Frank Elderson: Taking action for nature – investing in economic resilience and prosperity
news.summary: The European Commission estimates that, if current levels of PFAS pollution in Europe continue until 2050, the cost to society could reach €440 billion over that period. Treating polluted water alone could cost more than €1 trillion. [ 7 ] And the effects differ across regions and sectors: agriculture here, manufacturing there and energy production somewhere else. news.title: President of the European Central Bank Christine Lagarde to step down in February
news.summary: 7 next year, nearly nine months before her term expires, she announced Thursday. Lagarde has led the central bank since July 2019, steering its policy responses to the Covid-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and a series of energy price shocks that sent inflation in the 21-nation euro area above 11%. The announcement came ahead of the ECB's latest monetary policy decision, due later on Thursday, in which it is expected to hold interest rates despite inflation in the 21-nation euro zone hitting a three-year high in September. Berenberg Chief Economist Holger Schmieding said that as well as the usual issues of monetary policy competence and regional balance, the ECB would need to consider who could deal with potential financial turbulence amid widening spreads in bond yields between member states.

Banks reported unchanged credit standards for loans to households for house purchase (net percentage of 0%) and a further net tightening for consumer credit and other lending to households (net percentage of 14%). For firms, the net tightening surpassed the expectations reported by banks in the previous survey round (5%). news.title: U.S. worker job engagement hits lowest level since 2011, new Gallup poll finds
news.summary: Thirty-seven percent said they strongly agreed that their supervisor or someone at work cared, down from 40% in the first half of the year and well below the Covid peak of 47% in March 2020. Gallup's quarterly polling of the workforce on engagement — which tracks workers’ focus, motivation and enthusiasm for their jobs — fell to its lowest level since 2011 in the third quarter of 2026. The 29% mark that employee engagement fell to in Q3 2026 was two percentage points lower quarter over quarter, breaking below a floor that had been set through the first half of the year. And according to Gallup's approach, the survey results represent a significant number of workers, with each percentage point representing about 1.6 million U.S. employees, or roughly 3.2 million fewer engaged workers quarter over quarter in Q3.

news.title: EU Rules Out New Climate Finance Pledges at COP31
news.summary: The European Union has ruled out new climate finance commitments at COP31 as rising energy costs strain budgets and developing countries push for increased funding. The European Union will not be making new climate finance commitments at the upcoming COP31 conference, climate commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said, as quoted by Bloomberg today, describing the possibility of further financial commitments for emission reduction as “dead in the water”. The EU and its member states provided €32.3 billion around $36 billion in public climate finance to developing countries in 2025, up roughly €600 million from 2024, according to official EU data. Indeed, in a recent letter to the UN’s climate chief Simon Stiell, a group of African countries said they would be demanding a tripling of climate adaptation finance commitments at the COP31.

news.title: Economie et environnement : « Il faut donner une valeur à ce qui n’a pas de prix pour éclairer nos choix collectifs »
news.summary: Dans des travaux expérimentaux publiés en 2024, l’Insee propose un ajustement du produit intérieur net (le PIB moins l’amortissement des équipements) pour tenir compte de la dégradation du capital climatique et de l’épuisement du budget carbone (la quantité maximale de CO₂ que l’on peut émettre pour espérer limiter le réchauffement climatique au niveau qu’on s’est fixé). L’ajustement, évalué à 4,1 % du produit intérieur net en 2023, intègre à la fois une estimation des dommages climatiques et la valeur implicite de la contrainte sur les émissions futures. A u cœur de nos difficultés à protéger l’environnement et à lutter contre le réchauffement climatique se trouve un paradoxe : ce qui n’est pas compté risque de ne pas peser dans les décisions. L’instrument de mesure principal de l’activité économique, le produit intérieur brut (PIB), mesure la production, et non la richesse au sens large ni le bien-être.

news.summary: Fears of new tariffs flare up from time to time when the US president goes off the rails – for instance, threatening to end US trade with countries with which it has a deficit unless the Federal Reserve cuts interest rates. A truce has cooled the trade conflict, but neither country has done anything to limit the outbreak of new hostilities Donald Trump ’s trade wars have largely fallen off the headlines. But the sense that the world’s two largest economies are plowing ahead into an overt economic conflagration has taken a back seat to other, more salient fears, about Trump ending American democracy, AI killing us all and stuff like that. Under the radar, the world is marching toward an economic war of potentially epic proportions, one that, history suggests, could well spill over into the real thing.

news.title: Stock market after midterm elections: What S&P 500 history shows

news.title: ECB wage tracker suggests slightly higher wage growth in first three quarters of 2027 compared with the full year of 2026
news.summary: Compared with the September 2026 data release , the headline wage tracker was revised upwards slightly for the second half of 2026 and for the first half of 2027, by around 0.1 percentage points on average. The European Central Bank (ECB) headline wage tracker, which covers active collective bargaining agreements with one-off payments smoothed over 12 months, indicates negotiated wage growth of 2.3% in 2026 (based on a coverage of 46.2% of employees in participating countries). The relatively low ECB wage tracker in the first half of 2026 still reflects the downward mechanical impact of one-off payments that were initially paid in the second half of 2024 and not repeated in the following year. The ECB wage tracker with unsmoothed one-off payments stands at 2.4% for the third quarter of 2027, down from 2.7% for the first half of 2027 and for 2026 as a whole.

news.title: Global refinery inputs fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 before modest recovery
news.summary: Global crude oil refinery inputs fell by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q26), or 6%, following the start of conflict in late February in the Middle East, according to data from Kpler. Throughput then increased by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter, primarily as refiners in the region adjusted to new trade flows.

Car parts maker Schaeffler said Tuesday it would cut 3,460 jobs and shutter five of its sites across Europe, blaming an "automotive industry crisis" amid a struggle against economic headwinds, overseas competition and technological change. Schaeffler's challenges are far from isolated, with new car registrations in the European Union down from 15.3 million units in 2019 to 10.8 million units in 2025.

news.title: UK and EU agree draft deal to scrap Brexit red tape over food exports
news.summary: Speaking during the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (Chogm) in Antigua and Barbuda, the prime minister said a UK-EU deal could add up to 0.4% extra on GDP. "And that's what I've been doing in recent weeks, leaning in, being positive, having a really constructive relationship with our European partners and hopefully we can land a good deal for Britain in terms of growth but also I hope more collaboration on controlling immigration." Jon Walsh, the chief executive and co-founder of Bio&Me, which makes granolas, mueslis and yoghurts, told BBC 5 Live the draft deal sounded like "really good news". Pressed on whether it would be acceptable for the UK to have its rules on food trade made by the EU, he said: "We're not in the EU, therefore we do have to work with them in a different way. "Returning to any form of alignment with Europe would crush Britain's competitiveness and force us to surrender sovereignty over trade policy, putting trade deals worth hundreds of billions of pounds at risk." The government has already announced a European Partnerships Bill which will provide a legal mechanism for the application of new EU rules and regulations.

news.title: ECB wage tracker suggests slightly higher wage growth in first three quarters of 2027 compared with the full year of 2026
news.summary: Compared with the September 2026 data release , the headline wage tracker was revised upwards slightly for the second half of 2026 and for the first half of 2027, by around 0.1 percentage points on average. The European Central Bank (ECB) headline wage tracker, which covers active collective bargaining agreements with one-off payments smoothed over 12 months, indicates negotiated wage growth of 2.3% in 2026 (based on a coverage of 46.2% of employees in participating countries). The relatively low ECB wage tracker in the first half of 2026 still reflects the downward mechanical impact of one-off payments that were initially paid in the second half of 2024 and not repeated in the following year. The ECB wage tracker with unsmoothed one-off payments stands at 2.4% for the third quarter of 2027, down from 2.7% for the first half of 2027 and for 2026 as a whole.

news.title: Global refinery inputs fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 before modest recovery
news.summary: Global crude oil refinery inputs fell by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q26), or 6%, following the start of conflict in late February in the Middle East, according to data from Kpler. Throughput then increased by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter, primarily as refiners in the region adjusted to new trade flows.

news.title: ECB wage tracker suggests slightly higher wage growth in first three quarters of 2027 compared with the full year of 2026
news.summary: Compared with the September 2026 data release , the headline wage tracker was revised upwards slightly for the second half of 2026 and for the first half of 2027, by around 0.1 percentage points on average. The European Central Bank (ECB) headline wage tracker, which covers active collective bargaining agreements with one-off payments smoothed over 12 months, indicates negotiated wage growth of 2.3% in 2026 (based on a coverage of 46.2% of employees in participating countries). The relatively low ECB wage tracker in the first half of 2026 still reflects the downward mechanical impact of one-off payments that were initially paid in the second half of 2024 and not repeated in the following year. The ECB wage tracker with unsmoothed one-off payments stands at 2.4% for the third quarter of 2027, down from 2.7% for the first half of 2027 and for 2026 as a whole.

news.title: Jensen Huang affair puts Nvidia's future at risk, with no clear successor to the renowned CEO
news.summary: Shares of Nvidia sank more than 5% on Monday, even as the broader market rallied sharply, after Huang acknowledged the affair in a message to staff on Sunday, and said that the board was launching an investigation into whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence agency. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's admission of an affair with a purported Chinese spy has raised questions about his future at the company, and what happens if the 63-year-old co-founder, who built the chipmaker into one of the most valuable businesses on the planet, is forced out. He owns just over 3% of the outstanding shares and is one of 11 members on a board that has no official chair. The board said it has "confidence in Jensen," and that it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." The New York Times first reported that the Chinese businesswoman was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the intelligence circulated in a memo among the Trump administration in the spring.

news.title: A massive trade in Nvidia just went off – here are the details
news.summary: In a trade about an hour after the opening bell that involved more than $100 million in options premium, someone exchanged an existing call spread for a more bullish position that captures the next five months of trading in Nvidia. 19 worth about $57 million – contracts the trader opened for a new long position while simultaneously selling the same number of 245-strike calls for the same expiry, lowering the cost of the trade by $10 million. If Nvidia stock reaches the short, 245-strike call, it would represent a nearly 40% rally and return the stock to its all-time high of $243, that was reached on October 6th. The trade was likely part of a "roll" down from an existing 210/255-strike call spread worth about $42 million that was closed out, according to SpotGamma analysis.

news.title: China wholesale inflation hits highest in more than four years as consumer measure slows
news.summary: Producer prices in China grew at the fastest rate since June 2022, accelerating for the third month in a row. Consumer inflation in China slowed to 0.7% in October, its first deceleration after two straight months of increases. Core inflation, which strips out food and energy prices, came in at 0.8%, down from the 1% seen in the month before. The PPI for October came in at 5.7%, compared to the 5.3% expected by economists polled by Reuters.

news.title: Jensen Huang affair puts Nvidia's future at risk, with no clear successor to the renowned CEO
news.summary: Shares of Nvidia sank more than 4% on Monday, even as the broader market rallied sharply, after Huang acknowledged the affair in a message to staff on Sunday, and said that the board was launching an investigation into whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence agency. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's admission of an affair with a purported Chinese spy has raised questions about his future at the company, and what happens if the 63-year-old co-founder, who built the chipmaker into one of the most valuable businesses on the planet, is forced out. He owns just over 3% of the outstanding shares and is one of 11 members on a board that has no official chair. The board said it has "confidence in Jensen," and that it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised." The New York Times first reported that the Chinese businesswoman was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the intelligence circulated in a memo among the Trump administration in the spring.

news.title: Jensen Huang’s image has been shattered. Could he be pushed out at Nvidia?
news.summary: While not a company executive, his wife, Lori Mills Huang, leads the family foundation which, as of 2024, controls over 60m Nvidia shares. Huang built Nvidia as a family business but after the co-founder had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, its board faces a difficult decision For more than 30 years, Jensen Huang has been the seemingly unshakable public face of Nvidia. He co-founded the company as a young engineer in 1993 and oversaw its growth into a multitrillion dollar chipmaker and bellwether of the AI industry at large. His children, Madison and Spencer, have taken leadership roles at the firm.

news.title: China wholesale inflation hits highest in more than four years as consumer measure slows
news.summary: Producer prices in China grew at the fastest rate since June 2022, accelerating for the third month in a row. Consumer inflation in China slowed to 0.7% in October, its first deceleration after two straight months of increases. Core inflation, which strips out food and energy prices, came in at 0.8%, down from the 1% seen in the month before. The PPI for October came in at 5.7%, compared to the 5.3% expected by economists polled by Reuters.

news.title: A massive trade in Nvidia just went off – here are the details
news.summary: In a trade about an hour after the opening bell that involved more than $100 million in options premium, someone exchanged an existing call spread for a more bullish position that captures the next five months of trading in Nvidia. 19 worth about $57 million – contracts the trader opened for a new long position while simultaneously selling the same number of 245-strike calls for the same expiry, lowering the cost of the trade by $10 million. If Nvidia stock reaches the short, 245-strike call, it would represent a nearly 40% rally and return the stock to its all-time high of $243, that was reached on October 6th. The trade was likely part of a "roll" down from an existing 210/255-strike call spread worth about $42 million that was closed out, according to SpotGamma analysis.

news.summary: Research presented in our 2021 monetary policy strategy review suggests that information about the new inflation target reached only around one in ten consumers in the months following its announcement. As a result of the 2021 monetary policy strategy review, the Governing Council adopted the symmetric two per cent inflation target. At the following monetary policy meeting (July 2021), it revised its rate forward guidance by linking the expected policy path more explicitly to the inflation outlook and realised progress in underlying inflation. In July 2022 the Governing Council moved away from the effective lower bound by raising the policy rate from minus 50 basis points to zero.
